parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High Risk. Federal document rules are in force: passports carry birth sex, X markers are not issued, and the Supreme Court let restrictions take effect, with documented passport confiscations and strandings. Entry refusal on any discrepancy is written into cable guidance, with a possible lifetime fraud bar. Documented federal custody harms include forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse in immigration detention, and corrections policy on trans inmates. The division adds universal school-ground restroom exposure binding visitors and removes its own gender-identity anti-discrimination remedy. Mitigating: federal courts have enjoined several orders, adults' surgery coverage was judicially protected, and no documented division-level arrests or extortion of adult visitors appear. No capital pathway is documented. Violence counts are undercount floors and carry no usable weight.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports show birth sex; X markers no longer issued; new applications processed only M/F. Passports confiscated or blocked, leaving travellers stranded. Entry cable refuses cases with document discrepancy and raises a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; federal suit pending; some orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ available.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country documents mismatching presentation trigger refusal, referral and fraud questioning before any local rule applies; the lifetime-bar route can follow discovery.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cut, hormones removed) and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts. A state arrest under a bathroom-trespass law (handcuffing, 24 hours in men's ward) is documented in another state, not the division.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some custody-harm reporting and litigation; no documented division-level custody protection for adults.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document or facility dispute can move into federal custody, where birth-sex or conversion-style treatment and abuse are documented; state trespass exposure exists elsewhere.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities. Division rule: school-ground restrooms and changing areas limited to birth-certificate sex, binding visitors; single-person option only as student accommodation with guardian consent. Division removed gender identity from civil rights statutes and bars localities from stronger protections.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-person alternative exists for students with guardian consent; no documented adult facility statute in the division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal prohibition and division school rule stack; an adult visitor on campus has no written alternative, and facility checks may coincide with document checks.

care_services.exposure: Federal proposed rule to bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care (not in force). Federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients. Division bans minors' gender-affirming care. Federal hostility to youth care services and funding.
care_services.protection: Division courts kept adult gender-affirming surgery coverage available (2019 ruling); adult care not restricted in the division by documented statute.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking exposes records to federal subpoena; a travelling minor cannot obtain care locally under the division's ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders frame gender-identity advocacy and trans-affirming schools as law-enforcement targets; cash reward for leadership of groups tied to 'radically pro-transgender' ideology; counterterrorism strategy names such groups as priorities. Official 'forbidden terms' list.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Stated disclaimer that counterterrorism powers will not target people who disagree; enjoined or contested orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Visible trans advocacy or association with trans-affirming groups can draw federal law-enforcement attention that a visitor encounters at entry or in custody.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minors fall under the school restroom rule and cannot get the single-person alternative without guardian consent. Federal directive to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition, including preferred names. Division minors' care ban. Instruction on gender identity barred K-6 in the division.
minors_guardians.protection: Guardian-consent single-person accommodation at schools; guardian presence can support accommodation requests.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a minor must seek consent for accommodation, which itself requires disclosure; school staff may be pressed by federal prosecution threats.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-level documented street violence, police targeting or extortion of adult visitors. Federal hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes. Violence counts are undercount floors and cannot be used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute applies; federal civil-rights protections nationwide in employment; public opinion split but not hostile enforcement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse for a visitor depends on the federal hate-crimes route; division-level civil recourse is removed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division offers no state remedy for refusal of service, housing or employment on gender identity. Federal passport suit pending; many federal orders contested. Enforcement of school facility rule against adult visitors not documented beyond statute wording. Classification of division's facility status unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have enjoined some orders; national civil-liberties litigation active; hate-crimes statute federal; marriage recognition nationwide.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Because remedies are contested and the legal position moves, the visitor cannot know which rules apply at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest: both have birth-sex housing with documented assault and solitary-confinement harm and a facility statute against cross-dressing presence. This case lacks the anchor's documented presentation arrests and recurrent prolonged detention in the division, so it sits slightly higher.

Similar: universal birth-sex-based exclusion or document refusal with no effective appeal. This case is lower because it adds documented custody sexual abuse, forced labour and stranding abroad, which exceed the anchor's exclusion-and-humiliation harms.

Similar universal reporting-style exposure with weak remedies. This case is comparable on remedy weakness but lower on custody harm, since the anchor's consequences are shelter and money loss rather than documented abuse in state custody.

parsed.synthesis: Universal exposures (passport sex-marker mismatch, school-ground restroom rule binding visitors, federal facility restrictions) reach every travelling trans adult and apply at entry and on campuses. Documented state custody harms in federal immigration detention and corrections policy raise severity beyond exclusion. The division removes its own gender-identity remedy, so no local recourse exists for refusal of service or housing. Mitigations are real but limited: federal courts enjoin some orders, a national hate-crimes statute applies, and no division-level arrests or extortion of adult visitors are documented. Adult surgery coverage stands. Overall a combined operative regime in the High Risk band, with no capital pathway documented and violence figures unusable.
